title: Bitcoin mining difficulty reaches new all-time high as hash
content:
TL;DR: As of February 01, 2026, Bitcoin's network hums with a robust hashrate of 842.82 EH/s, actively securing the monetary base layer at a difficulty of 146.47 T. While not an all-time high, this computational power underscores Bitcoin's unwavering commitment to decentralized, censorship-resistant money, especially as the next difficulty adjustment looms with a likely downward correction, signaling miner adaptation. For transactors, this period demands strategic attention to transaction timing and an understanding of the protocol's self-regulating genius in the face of global economic shifts.

The Report

Good morning, transactors. It is February 01, 2026, at 06:39 UTC, and the Bitcoin network remains a beacon of computational integrity, relentlessly processing transactions and securing the hardest money ever invented. We've seen the network maintain a formidable operational status, with the current block height standing at 934,564. This continuous, unbroken chain of blocks is a testament to the protocol's resilience and the global dedication of miners. However, the narrative often spun by mainstream outlets about "record highs" often misses the nuanced reality of Bitcoin's dynamic difficulty adjustment mechanism.

Today, the network's hashrate registers at 842.82 EH/s. This is a significant amount of computational power, representing a vast expenditure of energy dedicated to validating the ledger and protecting its integrity. For context, the difficulty setting, which was last adjusted on January 23, 2026, stands at 146.47 T. It is crucial to note that this figure is not an all-time high. The network experienced a peak difficulty of 155.9 T in November 2025, demonstrating that current conditions, while strong, are part of a larger, fluctuating cycle of miner participation and technological advancement. The network continuously adapts, proving its anti-fragile design.
